name: Tremella fuciformis

ecology.substrate: the mycelium of a wood-decay ascomycete, on dead broadleaf wood

notes: A parasite of another fungus, from a separate class (Tremellomycetes). Reported (unchecked) to have a yeast phase plus hyphae that tap the host's hyphae, to be cultivated in China as a two-fungus culture and to have a sequenced genome.

tip_speed.note: Claude's inference from the species' ecology and general knowledge, not from a measurement (2026-11-10): grows as slow yeast-like cells and thin hyphae, and only fruits beside its host fungus

uptake_rate.note: tuning value, set to tip speed / segment length so that one feeding segment can supply about one growing tip; no measurement found
